*21. (a) Prove that there does not exist a continuous function f defined on R
which takes on every value exactly twice. Hint: If f(a) = f(b) for
a < b, then either /(x) > f(a) for all x in (a,b) or /(x) < f(a) for
all x in (a, b). Why? In the first case all values close to f(a), but slightly
larger than f(a\ are taken on somewhere in (a, b); this implies that
/(x) < f(a) for x < a and x > b.
(b) Refine part (a) by proving that there is no continuous function f which
takes on each value either 0 times or 2 times, i.e., which takes on exactly
twice each value that it does take on. Hint: The previous hint implies
that f has either a maximum or a minimum value (which must be taken
on twice). What can be said about values close to the maximum value?
(c) Find a continuous function f which takes on every value exactly 3 times.
More generally, find one which takes on every value exactly n times, if
n is odd.
(d) Prove that if n is even, then there is no continuous f which takes on
every value exactly n times. Hint: To treat the case n = 4, for example,
let /(xi) = /(X2) = /(X3) = /(X4). Then either /(x) > 0 for all x in
two of the three intervals (xi, X2), (X2, X3), (X3, X4), or else /(x) < 0 for
all x in two of these three intervals.
